column1: # roots.tsv — every named root, and the base it hangs off. harbor#630.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Measured 2026-09-23: 91 non-comment, non-markdown lines
# in this repo name a repo root, and 13 of them go through a `${VAR:-...}`
# override. The other 78 are bare literals, and the 13 that are not disagree
# with each other — PROJECT_INIT_SRC and HARBOR_PROJECT_INIT are two variables
# for one repo with one default. Nothing checked any of it against anything, so
# every default read correctly at every site while drifting from its siblings.
# THE BASE COLUMN IS THE POINT. A root is `<base>/<rel>`, and `base` is symbolic:
# REPOS is where the governed repositories live. It was $HOME until harbor#619
# moved them on 2026-09-23, and is $HOME/port since — ONE edit in bin/roots.sh,
# not thirteen across the tree. BOX is the per-machine config tier and never moves.
# ENFORCED by lint ROOT1, which reads this file and refuses a default in the
# tree that disagrees with it. Without that rule this is another copy, and a
# copy is the thing it was written to remove.
# HONOURS PORT_ROOT. `roots.sh --get`, `--list` and `--repos` resolve a REPOS row under
# an exported PORT_ROOT (default $HOME/port) and a BOX row under $HOME, and an exported
# <var> still wins over both. A site spells the same default as
# ${VAR:-${PORT_ROOT:-$HOME/port}/<rel>}: --check reads that nested form, compares it
# with this table, and REFUSES the flat form ${VAR:-$HOME/port/<rel>} for a REPOS row,
# because the flat form answers $HOME/port on a machine whose workspace is elsewhere.
# TWO NAMES FOR ONE PATH ARE A DECISION, NOT A DRIFT. --check refuses rows that share a
# path unless every one of them carries a reason in the fifth column (a # cannot appear
# in it: a # starts a comment). PROJECT_INIT_SRC and HARBOR_PROJECT_INIT are such a pair:
# merging them changes an env contract (suites and operators set either by hand), so the
# names stay and the reason is recorded rather than a merge being done in passing.
# COLUMNS  var <TAB> base <TAB> rel <TAB> what breaks when it is wrong <TAB> why a shared path is deliberate (only when shared)
var
